# CueNow 1.4.53
## Fixes
- Fixed CueNow's menu bar icon hiding when ChatGPT, Cursor, Claude, or another application's menu bar item is turned off in System Settings on macOS 26. - Each application's System Settings switch now controls only that application's menu bar icon, including CueNow's own switch. - CueNow now uses macOS's native menu bar registration as the single source of truth for visibility, preventing the runaway scene-update loop seen in 1.4.51 and 1.4.52. - The Hide dock icon preference now takes effect after reopening CueNow so the menu bar registration remains stable.

# CueNow 1.4.52
## Fixes
- Fixed the CueNow menu bar icon disappearing after changing other apps' menu bar settings on macOS 26. - CueNow now uses one standard 22-point menu bar slot instead of reserving a 43-point variable-width slot, so macOS no longer pushes it out while rearranging a crowded menu bar.

# CueNow 1.4.51
## Fixes
- Fixed the CueNow menu bar icon disappearing when another app's icon was hidden from System Settings on macOS 26. CueNow's menu bar item had no name of its own, so macOS grouped it with every other unnamed menu bar item — including Cursor, Codex and Claude — under a single shared visibility switch. - CueNow's menu bar icon now has its own visibility switch and is unaffected by other apps. Its position in the menu bar is preserved when updating. - Corrected the migration for people who had already turned off the shared menu bar item before installing 1.4.51. CueNow now restores its icon once after taking ownership of its unique visibility setting, then preserves any later choice to hide CueNow itself.
